turnaround_reason: Everforth (the former ASGN, renamed April 2026) is down ~52% over the past year on a soft IT-staffing cycle and weak federal demand. The recovery pitch is a pivot from traditional staffing toward higher-value cloud/data/AI/cybersecurity consulting, which is expanding margins.
bullish_points: Q2 beat: revenue >$1B and adjusted EBITDA margin 9.6%, both above the high end of guidance
AI/cloud pivot has real proof points: expanded AWS Premier partnership; Navy 'Harbinger' AI-sonar program and DHS cybersecurity work in Federal
Cheap: forward P/E ~7.5, EV/EBITDA 7.8, P/B 0.73, EV/revenue 0.67; solid FCF ~$214M
Cluster of insider open-market buys in April 2026 (~$18.9-22.7), including a director at 10,000 shares (~$193k)
bearish_points: Federal segment is weak: book-to-bill only 0.7x; overall revenue declining (-1.3% TTM)
Analyst mean target $27.50 sits BELOW the current $32.39 - the Street implies downside from here
Stock has already nearly doubled off the $16.90 52w low to $32.39 (+33% above 100d MA) but is still under its 200d MA - extended within a still-unconfirmed base
Q1 FY26 showed margin compression (gross 27.5%, EBITDA 8.6%) before Q2 recovered; recovery is choppy
Options are effectively illiquid (call OI ~996, put OI ~551, near-zero sampled IV) - spot only
catalyst: Q3 earnings showing sustained margin expansion and any inflection in Federal book-to-bill back above 1.0x
suggested_trade: Spot only, small starter and only on a pullback toward the low-$20s insider-buy zone; entering here at $32 chases a doubled stock into a Street target below price
key_risk: Federal demand stays depressed and the staffing cycle doesn't recover, so the guided consulting-mix margin story fails to offset declining revenue
would_skip_if: Entry is above ~$28 (already past mean target) or Federal book-to-bill deteriorates further on the next print
